subject.title: feat: heading-aware chunking + entity extraction for memory search

question: Should OpenClaw make markdown heading-aware memory chunking the default behavior, add an explicit opt-in chunking strategy, or defer chunking until the broader Memory MVP/entity design is settled?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix changes persisted index identity and user retrieval behavior, while the same issue also bundles a larger entity/graph-memory direction.

options.title: Split And Approve Narrow Chunking
options.body: Keep this issue canonical, implement heading-aware chunking as a focused memory-core change with explicit reindex semantics, and track entity extraction separately.

options.title: Make Heading-Aware Default
options.body: Adopt heading boundaries as canonical markdown memory behavior, accepting that existing headed files will reindex and retrieve differently.

options.title: Defer To Memory MVP
options.body: Keep this open but wait for memory write/entity pipeline decisions so chunking, extraction, and wiki synthesis land as one coordinated design.

recommendation.title: Split And Approve Narrow Chunking
recommendation.body: Keep this issue canonical, implement heading-aware chunking as a focused memory-core change with explicit reindex semantics, and track entity extraction separately.

likelyOwner.reason: Current memory-core and memory-wiki blame/history make this the best available owner for the combined chunking and entity-extraction product boundary choice.
